trust_decision.summary: sqlite3_deserialize is called with SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_READONLY and without FREEONCLOSE, so SQLite keeps the caller's buffer pointer for the whole life of the connection; the public wrapper passes a borrowed &[u8] whose owner (a SerializedDatabase freed with sqlite3_free, or any Rust Vec) may drop immediately after the call, so the fix moves the lifetime decision into SqliteConnection by copying the bytes into a connection-owned Vec<u8>.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names SqliteConnection::deserialize_readonly_database_from_buffer; it is the only public deserialize entry and the only caller of the raw primitive, so an engineer who read only the summary starts here.

fix_sites.entry_point: SqliteConnection struct (new owning field serialized_data; ordering relative to raw_connection is load-bearing)
SqliteConnection::establish -> establish_inner (constructor must initialise the new field)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2/O8 site exists; the nearest dismissal a solver could use is for the crate-private primitive itself - RawConnection::deserialize is pub(super) and RawConnection is never exposed, so nothing outside diesel/src/sqlite/connection/mod.rs can reach the sink and the caller-side copy is 'enough'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Connection teardown must still read the deserialized pages: RawConnection::drop calls sqlite3_close while the pager still points at the buffer, so the owning Vec<u8> has to be declared after raw_connection (Rust drops fields in declaration order). A fix that puts the new field first, or that hands ownership to SQLite via SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_FREEONCLOSE, breaks close (and frees Rust-allocated memory with sqlite3_free / double-frees a SerializedDatabase).

O6_input_shapes: borrowed &[u8] from SerializedDatabase::as_slice() - sqlite3_malloc'd memory released by sqlite3_free in Drop (diesel/src/sqlite/connection/serialized_database.rs:28-31,42-49)
borrowed &[u8] from any Rust-owned Vec<u8>/file read, dropped right after the call
'static slices (include_bytes!), which never needed the copy
empty slice / length that does not fit sqlite3_int64 (error path still stores the copy) (diesel/src/sqlite/connection/raw.rs:236-239)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second public wrapper over RawConnection::deserialize (e.g. SqliteConnection::from_serialized_database(&SerializedDatabase) or a fixture loader) that forwards the borrowed slice without copying.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The raw layer already takes a plain &[u8] and encodes the 'buffer must outlive the connection' contract only in the new field, so any new thin wrapper added later inherits the same trap; diesel's style is one thin wrapper per convenience (mod.rs:624 vs raw.rs:218).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second consecutive call to deserialize_readonly_database_from_buffer (swap databases on a live connection): self.serialized_data = data.to_vec() frees the previous buffer before sqlite3_deserialize re-points the pager at the new one.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Re-using one connection to load a second snapshot is the obvious runtime use of this API, and the fix's own comment only reasons about the connection-lifetime case, not replacement.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A blob/open-statement handle retaining a pager that is pointing at a buffer the connection no longer owns.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The read-only blob type already hands out handles onto the main database; a maintainer adding 'reload the database' support would have to think about it explicitly.

O9_family: CWE-416 use-after-free: FFI borrow of a caller-owned buffer (sqlite3_deserialize with READONLY, no copy) outliving the Rust borrow

O10_build.toolchain: cargo / rustc >= 1.88.0, edition 2024 (Cargo.toml:40-42); libsqlite3-sys >= 0.30.1,<0.38.0 with bundled_bindings (diesel/Cargo.toml:54), optional 'bundled' feature via __with_asan_tests (diesel/Cargo.toml:101-108); the sqlite backend requires --features sqlite (__sqlite-shared, diesel/Cargo.toml:100)
O10_build.project_tests: unit test database_serializes_and_deserializes_successfully (diesel/src/sqlite/connection/mod.rs:1122-1155) uses an in-memory connection (mod.rs:842-844), so no server is needed: cargo test -p diesel --features sqlite sqlite::connection; an ASan build exists via the __with_asan_tests feature, which is what would actually detect this UAF.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Pass SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_FREEONCLOSE (or drop SQLITE_DESERIALIZE_READONLY) so SQLite 'owns' the buffer - which frees a SerializedDatabase twice or runs sqlite3_free on Rust memory - instead of copying the bytes into a field declared after raw_connection.

out_of_scope_notes: Adjacent, not this advisory: the SQLite bind path also uses SQLITE_STATIC with a Rust-owned Box kept alive next to the statement (diesel/src/sqlite/connection/stmt.rs:105-158); separate lifetime contract, not pursued.
unverified: Repo size in MB not measured (no shell), so tiny_repo/giant_repo was not assessed; diesel is clearly larger than 5 MB.
Present-in-latest is unknown for everything (no latest release provided for O8).

Whether a second call to deserialize_readonly_database_from_buffer actually touches the freed previous buffer inside sqlite3_deserialize/sqlite3_close could not be checked without running SQLite; the O8b entry for it is therefore a candidate, not a confirmed uncovered route.

The existing test at diesel/src/sqlite/connection/mod.rs:1122-1155 is the same test function the fix extends, but the asserting lines the fix adds (std::mem::drop + requery) are absent at the pinned commit, so regression_tests_in_pinned_commit was not set; a solver can still see the test area.
